# Delta correctness verdict: PASS-WITH-NOTES

PR #194 at `52cb3642755ca0dcd325fcafd8a029583f706b06`, answering `01a1bd0d-7737-7e70-ad34-69150a562f76`. **F001 and F002 from output 1291a64 are closed.** No new correctness blocker.

**F001:** one `notice_kinds!` invocation now generates the enum, ALL and the exhaustive prefix match (`crates/core/src/notice_id.rs:19-111`). The source-to-compiled test independently reads that invocation and compares its names, order and prefix bytes with the compiled table (`crates/daemon/tests/notice_ids.rs:376-398`). A kind cannot be declared separately while silently omitted from the normal generated ALL. The retained R2-M1 mutation deliberately drops a compiled entry and fails this comparison; the ordinary refusal test remained green under that mutation, correctly demonstrating why it was insufficient alone.

**F002:** SidecarBg owns `bg-`, and both background-sidecar cancellation and terminal mints now use it (`notice_id.rs:49-50`; `crates/sidecars/src/background.rs:321,435`). Their emitted bytes remain `bg-<id>-cancelled` and `bg-<id>-terminal`. All 29 previous table prefixes are unchanged; the table now has 30 kinds. The withdrawal-retry regression also passed.

Ordinary next_message_id/shim message IDs remain outside this reserved-notice scope, as the PR explicitly records for follow-up. The already documented possible duplicate on an upgrade-spanning old withdrawal retry remains unchanged.
